alerts.message: A creatinine result appears only in pasted lab text, so its date is unknown. Check when it was taken and enter it as a dated lab result for a patient on TDF.

alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF in pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF is associated with renal toxicity including elevated creatinine. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL and eGFR dropped to 78 mL/min/1.73m² within 10 weeks of starting TDF. Pregnancy itself increases renal workload, and TDF can compound this. Against drug attribution: the rise is modest, urinalysis is normal without proteinuria, and phosphate remains normal. However, the trend warrants close monitoring as pregnancy progresses. TDF-related renal effects can worsen over time.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor creatinine and eGFR monthly during pregnancy. If creatinine continues rising or eGFR falls below 60, consider switching TDF to alternative NRTI such as ABC or AZT.

alerts.title: DTG and iron supplement interaction
alerts.message: DTG requires separation from divalent cation-containing supplements including iron. Patient is taking ferrous sulfate and folic acid prescribed during pregnancy. Co-administration without temporal separation can significantly reduce DTG absorption and compromise viral suppression. Patient's viral load is currently 89 copies/mL, suggesting current administration may be adequate, but adherence to timing is critical to maintain suppression.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to take ferrous sulfate at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after DTG. Verify current dosing schedule and reinforce at every visit.

alerts.title: Missing VL monitoring per pregnancy schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring at 3-month intervals during pregnancy. Patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago with baseline VL of 125,000 copies/mL. Current VL of 89 copies/mL is excellent, but no clinician plan is documented for repeat VL timing. Guidelines call for repeat VL at 3 months post-initiation in pregnancy, and additional VL at delivery if gestation exceeds 28 weeks.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule repeat viral load at 3 months post-ART initiation and at delivery. Document monitoring plan in patient record.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this pregnant patient on ART for 10 weeks. Key clinical decisions are missing: renal monitoring plan for rising creatinine on TDF, DTG-iron separation counselling, scheduling of repeat viral load per pregnancy guidelines, and evaluation of the 6kg weight gain. Documentation gaps risk delayed intervention for renal decline or treatment failure.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment addressing renal trend, drug-supplement timing, VL monitoring schedule, and weight gain evaluation before patient leaves today.

etween DTG and divalent cation-containing medication in pregnancy, since pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements and/or magnesium-/aluminium- containing antacids (see module 17). Patients returning to care in pregnancy after interrupting a first-line NNRTI regimen or those exposed to previous VTP regimens should be put directly on a DTG-based regimen, rather than retrying an NNRTI-regimen (see also module 16).
